answerHtml:
2.

Compare the vapour pressure and density of liquid water to the other named substances. Justify the reasoning behind your prediction, using diagrams where appropriate.

a. Compared the pentane (C5H12), the vapour pressure of liquid water is: (3 marks)

higher equal lower

Explanation:
The hydrogen bonding in water is much stronger than the dispersion forces in pentane. As a result, at a given temperature there will be less evaporated water than evaporated pentane, resulting in less gas pressure from the evaporated water molecules.

Lower (1 marks)

Recognises there is a difference in strength of bonding
(hydrogen bonding vs dispersion forces) (1 marks)

Shows understanding between vapour pressure and IMF (1 marks)

(Total: 3 marks marks)

b. Compared the solid water (ice), the density of liquid water is: (4 marks)

higher equal lower

Liquid water and solid water both have hydrogen bonding. In solid ice this hydrogen bonding causes particles to arrange in a way which maximises this bonding (see diagram). This configuration places molecules further apart, resulting in the solid having lower density than the liquid

Higher (1 marks)

Recognises that both substances have hydrogen bonds (1 marks)

Recognises that the arrangement of hydrogen bonds in solid ice results in lower density (1 marks)

Appropriate diagram (1 marks)

(Total: 4 marks marks)

Water has hydrogen bonding (1 marks)

The weak dispersion forces results in a relatively low boiling point (1 marks)

A group of students wanted to measure the rate of reaction between magnesium and hydrochloric acid at different temperatures. The equation for the reaction is:

Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl2 + H2

In order to avoid conflicting results, the students wanted to ensure that they had sufficient acid to react with all of the magnesium.

What volume of 0.1 mol/L acid would be required to completely react with 1 g strips of magnesium?

(3 marks)

n(Mg) = m/M = 1 / 24.31 = 0.0411 mol (1 marks)

n(HCl) = 2 x n(Mg) = 0.08227 mol (1 marks)

c = n / V

V = n / C

= 0.08227 / 0.1 = 0.823 L (823 mL)

(1 marks)

answerHtml:
Teacher review required. The supplied 90 ppm answer conflicts with the plotted calibration line: peak area 12,000 corresponds to approximately 125–130 ppm. Review before marking.
